chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who speaks during his Adhan or his Iqamah, and he said, 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the Adhan or Iqamah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that casual speech during the Adhan or Iqamah does not invalidate the call, reflecting the Shia view that these acts are recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory pillars (arkan). This ruling facilitates practical ease for the caller, distinguishing between essential components and non-essential elements of the ritual. It underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the performance of recommended acts, provided the core intent and structure remain intact.
